1	# Marketing Agency — Architecture & Build Plan
2	
3	**Author:** Research/architecture agent · **Date:** 2026-08-10
4	**Status:** Research + planning only. No code written, nothing deployed, no APIs mutated.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. Product Overview
9	
10	A **productized web-design agency as software**. Two halves:
11	
12	1. **Demo-Gen Engine (flagship, the wedge):** Pick a business vertical (dentist, restaurant, gym, law firm, salon, HVAC, med-spa, auto shop…) → load a vertical-specific site template → take a target business from a prospect list → scrape/read its *current* website → extract brand (logo, colors, copy, services, hours, reviews) → generate a demonstrably *better* AI-built site → deploy it to a per-prospect subdomain (`joes-diner.demos.agency-domain.com`) → hand the link to the **Cold Email Engine** (separate product) for outreach: *"We built you a free redesign — here it is."* When they click, a **claim/CTA flow** captures the warm lead.
13	2. **Agency CRM / Pipeline:** Once a prospect replies, the demo becomes a deal. Pipeline (Lead → Demo Sent → Opened → Replied → Call → Won → Onboarding → Live → Retainer), proposals/contracts, billing, and handoff (promote the demo to a real, owned site).
14	
15	It ships **standalone** (`agency.<domain>`) *and* as a **Nxeon admin add-on module** (`/admin/agency`), because Nxeon is the central hub and already owns the hosting infra the demos deploy onto.
16	
17	### Core value chain
18	`Vertical + Template Library` × `AI Generation` × `Cheap per-prospect Deploy` × `Personalized Outreach` = high-conversion lead-gen. The moat is **volume + personalization + the demo already exists** — the prospect sees the finished product, not a pitch.

22	## 2. Competitors & Positioning
23	
24	| Product | What it is | Price | Relevance |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| **Durable** | GPT-driven 30-sec site builder for local service businesses | ~$12–15/mo | Closest to our *generation* quality bar; all-in-one but generic templates. |
27	| **B12** | AI site in ~60s + human-assisted service tier | $42–$399/mo | Hybrid AI+expert; our "won client" tier competes here. |
28	| **10Web** | AI → full WordPress + managed hosting, Elementor editor | $10–20/mo+ | Proves AI→editable→hosted pipeline; WP lock-in. |
29	| **Framer AI / v0 (Vercel)** | AI generates high-design React/Framer sites | v0 $20/mo (5k credits); Framer usage-based | Best-in-class *output quality*; not an agency/outreach engine. |
30	| **Readdy / LeadGen.ai / ManyRequests-style "spec site" plays** | Auto-generate a personalized demo per lead + link it in outreach | agency SaaS pricing | **Direct competitor to our exact play** — validates the model. |
31	
32	**Positioning:** We are *not* selling a DIY builder. We sell **done-for-you demos at scale that convert cold prospects**, backed by a real agency pipeline + Nxeon hosting. Differentiators: (a) **per-vertical designed template library** (not generic), (b) **real brand extraction** from the prospect's existing site so the demo feels bespoke, (c) **owned hosting** = near-zero marginal deploy cost, (d) integrated CRM→billing→handoff, (e) tight loop with the Cold Email Engine.

58	## 4. Recommended Tech Stack
59	
60	- **Framework:** Next.js 15 App Router + TypeScript (matches Nxeon exactly; shares `components/portal/Shell.tsx`, `components/ui/`, `app/globals.css` design system).
61	- **DB:** PostgreSQL + Prisma. Standalone gets its own DB; as add-on, additive tables in the Nxeon schema (prefix `agency_` / `Agency*` models, mirroring how shared-hosting added `HostingNode`/`HostingAccount` without touching the VPS models).
62	- **Generation:** Anthropic SDK with **structured output** (JSON Schema / tool-use) to emit a validated **Site IR** (page → sections → blocks with typed props), *not* raw HTML. Deterministic renderer maps IR → React components from the vertical template. This is the 2026 best practice (structured output over free-form HTML — Outlines/tool-use) and keeps output on-brand and safe.
63	- **Rendering the demo:** Two options — (A) **static export** of the generated site (Next static/HTML) served as a plain vhost on a Nxeon shared node (cheapest, safest, no runtime); (B) a single multi-tenant Next app that renders by subdomain from stored IR. **MVP = (A) static export** (near-zero cost, trivially cacheable, no per-demo process).
64	- **Background work:** a worker/queue mirroring Nxeon's `HostingTask`/worker-tick pattern (jobs: `SCRAPE`, `GENERATE`, `RENDER`, `DEPLOY`, `SCREENSHOT`, `NOTIFY_OUTREACH`). Status-driven state machine so a demo self-completes and retries.

Capture HTML, full-page screenshot, and (Firecrawl `/extract` or Brandfetch) structured brand: **logo, palette, fonts, headings, services, hours, address, phone, review snippets**. Respect robots/ToS (§11). Store `BrandProfile`.
98	3. **Normalize + classify.** Cheap Haiku call: confirm vertical, summarize services, pull a value-prop, flag if the current site is missing (a *no-site* prospect is an even better target — generate from Places data only).
99	4. **Plan.** Sonnet call with **structured output** → **Site IR**: choose sections from the vertical template's `sectionCatalog` (hero, services grid, about, testimonials, gallery, booking CTA, map, FAQ, footer), write on-brand copy, map extracted colors→theme tokens (with contrast/accessibility guardrails), pick imagery. Validate IR against JSON Schema; reject/repair invalid.
100	5. **Render.** Deterministic renderer: IR + template React components + theme tokens → **static HTML/CSS** export. No prospect logo re-hosted verbatim if legal flag set — use their name in brand type + a neutral/generated mark (§11). Inject a discreet **"Demo by <Agency> — not affiliated with <Business>"** disclaimer + a **claim CTA**.
101	6. **QA gate.** Automated checks: valid HTML, Lighthouse/perf, no broken links, contrast, no profanity/hallucinated claims, required disclaimer present. Optional human-approve queue before it can be sent.
102	7. **Deploy.** Provision subdomain on Nxeon (§7), publish static files, issue SSL, warm cache. Store `deployUrl`.
103	8. **Screenshot before/after.** Render a side-by-side (their old site vs. our new) for the outreach email.
104	9. **Hand to Cold Email Engine.** Emit `demo.ready` webhook/event with `{prospect, deployUrl, beforeAfterImg, claimUrl}`. Cold Email Engine owns sending. We only track opens/clicks via the claim link + a tracking pixel/redirect we host.
105	10. **Warm-lead capture.** Claim page (`/claim/<token>`) = "Love it? Book a call / make it yours." Fires `DemoEvent` → creates/advances a `Deal`.
106	11. **Lifecycle.** Demos **auto-expire** (e.g. 30 days) and are torn down to reclaim subdomains and reduce brand-exposure risk unless converted.
107	
108	---
109	
110	## 7. Deploy / Hosting — Reuse Nxeon Infra
111	
112	Nxeon **already has** everything needed (per shared-hosting build):
113	- **Shared-hosting nodes** (`HostingNode`, e.g. `hosting-1` on a dedicated public IP) with **name-based nginx vhosts** routing by Host header — perfect for many demos on one IP.
114	- **Per-domain SSL via SNI + certbot-webroot** auto-issue once DNS resolves — reuse for `*.demos.<domain>`.
115	- **Worker task queue** (`HostingTask`/worker-tick) pattern to copy for demo jobs.
116	- **Namecheap DNS** lib to create the one-time wildcard `*.demos.<domain>` A record → node IP.
117	- **Catch-all default vhost** already exists so an unmatched host never leaks.
118	
119	**Demo deploy = the cheapest possible case of shared hosting:** a static-file vhost, no PHP-FPM, no DB, no jailed shell. Recommended path: add a lightweight **`agency-demo` provisioner** that (1) writes a name-based nginx vhost `sub.demos.<domain>` → static dir, (2) drops the exported HTML, (3) reuses the existing **SSL sweep** for SNI cert, (4) reuses the **catch-all** for safety. This slots into the existing worker with **zero new hosting vendor** and marginal cost ≈ disk + a cert. Wildcard cert (`*.demos.<domain>` via DNS-01) is an alternative to per-host SNI if demo volume is high — Coolify/Traefik or certbot DNS plugin both do this; Nxeon's Namecheap creds enable the DNS-01 challenge.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## 8. Standalone AND Nxeon Add-on
124	
125	**Shared core:** a `packages/agency-core` (or a plain internal lib) holding the pipeline, IR schema, renderer, template library, and provisioner interface — deployment-target-agnostic.
126	
127	- **Standalone app** (`agency.<domain>`, own Next app + own Postgres on dev box `51.79.226.215`): full marketing site + app; deploy adapter talks to a Nxeon HostingNode over the same SSH/provisioner contract (or its own VPS). Own auth/billing.
128	- **Nxeon add-on** (`/admin/agency` + optional customer `/dashboard/agency`): additive `Agency*` Prisma models in the Nxeon schema (never touch VPS/hosting models — same discipline as shared-hosting), reuse `Shell.tsx`, `components/ui/`, Stripe, Namecheap, the worker, and the **existing Board** (`/admin/board`) for the pipeline UI. Feature-flag `ENABLE_AGENCY=1`, inert until reviewed — exactly the shared-hosting pattern.
129	
130	Design one **provisioner interface** + one **outreach interface** so both surfaces share code; only the host wiring differs.
131	
132	---
133	
134	## 9. Phased Build Plan
135	
136	**Phase 0 — Spike (no prod):** IR schema + one vertical template (e.g. dentist) + Claude structured-output plan→render to static HTML locally. Manual scrape of one *consented* test site. Prove quality bar.
137	
138	**Phase 1 — MVP (the flagship loop, single vertical, human-in-loop):**
139	- 1 vertical, 1–2 templates, section catalog + theme tokens.
140	- Scrape (Playwright) + brand extract (Brandfetch/Firecrawl) → BrandProfile.
141	- Claude gen → validated IR → static render → QA gate → **manual approve**.
142	- Deploy to `sub.demos.<domain>` via Nxeon vhost + SNI SSL.
143	- Before/after screenshot; emit `demo.ready` to Cold Email Engine (stub if not ready).
144	- Claim page + event tracking. Minimal admin list of demos.
145	- **Legal guardrails on from day one** (disclaimer, no verbatim logo re-host by default, allow/deny list, opt-out/takedown, auto-expire).
146	
147	**Phase 2 — Scale & verticals:** 5–10 verticals, template library tooling, Firecrawl at volume, batch generation (Anthropic Batch API for cost), auto-approve for high-confidence, wildcard cert, bulk import from Places, dashboards/analytics (open→click→claim→won funnel).
148	
149	**Phase 3 — Agency CRM/billing/handoff:** full pipeline (reuse Board), proposals/contracts (e-sign), Stripe retainers, **handoff** = promote demo to a real owned Nxeon hosting account + custom domain, client dashboard, white-label for sub-agencies.
150	
151	**Phase 4 — Optimization:** A/B templates, learn which designs convert, self-serve tenant onboarding, generated hero imagery, multi-language.
152	
153	---
154	
155	## 10. Key Risks
156	
157	1. **Legal/brand exposure (biggest)** — see §11. Unsolicited use of a business's logo/brand in a live public demo is the single largest risk; mitigations are mandatory, not optional.
158	2. **Email deliverability & spam law** — outreach volume can nuke sending domains and trip CAN-SPAM/GDPR/CASL. Owned by Cold Email Engine, but our demo links/domains share reputation; keep demo domain separate from sending domain, honor opt-out, throttle.
159	3. **Generation quality variance** — a bad demo hurts the brand and the pitch. Mitigate with QA gate + human approve early + structured IR (not free HTML).
160	4. **Cost blow-ups** — Firecrawl `/extract` and Opus can get pricey at volume; default to Playwright + Sonnet/Haiku + Batch; cap per-prospect spend.
161	5. **Hosting abuse/reputation** — many auto-generated sites on shared IPs can look spammy to Google Safe Browsing; use `noindex` on demos, `robots: disallow`, isolate demo IP from production customer IPs.
162	6. **Scraping breakage / anti-bot** — sites block scrapers; Firecrawl fallback + graceful "generate from Places data only."
163	7. **Multi-tenant data isolation** if sold to sub-agencies.
164	
165	---

167	## 11. Legal / Ethical / Compliance (MANDATORY)
168	
169	- **Trademark — nominative fair use.** Using a business's **plain-text name** to identify them (in the demo + outreach) is generally defensible nominative fair use: (a) they can't be identified without the name, (b) use only as much as necessary, (c) do nothing implying sponsorship/endorsement. **Using their distinctive logo, exact font, or full color scheme is riskier** — courts treat visual branding as more likely to imply endorsement and as "more than necessary." **Rule:** default to *name in type + a neutral/AI-generated mark + a palette inspired-by (not identical)*; only re-host their actual logo with consent. (INTA, Chase Law, Nolo, Davis+Gilbert.)
170	- **Copyright.** Their site copy/images are their (or a third party's) copyright. Don't republish verbatim; **rewrite** copy (we do — it's a *redesign*) and use **our/licensed/generated imagery**, not scraped photos. Logos may also be copyrighted separately from TM.

## Sitewave Phase 2 — done

Worked exclusively in the isolated worktree `/opt/nxeon-build` on branch `feature/agency-sitewave-phase2` (verified `pwd`/branch before building; ran its own `npm ci`). No prod paths touched, no systemctl/deploy, no `prisma db push`, no `.env` edits.

### Files added
- **`lib/agency/scrape.ts`** — SSRF-safe scrape + extraction.
- **`lib/agency/deploy.ts`** — pure static-bundle builder + `agency_deploy_enabled` gate helper.
- **`app/admin/agency/pipeline/page.tsx`** — CRM kanban.
- **`app/admin/agency/prospects/[id]/page.tsx`** — prospect detail (activity log, scrape result, demos, deal controls, client + quotes).
- **`test/agency-phase2.test.ts`** — 26 tests.

### Files changed
`lib/actions-agency.ts` (new guarded actions), `components/admin/agency/Controls.tsx` (pipeline/quote/scrape UI), `lib/settings.ts` (`agency_deploy_enabled`, default `false`), `lib/rbac.ts` + `lib/admin-groups.ts` (pipeline route/nav), `app/admin/agency/{demos,prospects}/page.tsx`, `prisma/schema.prisma` (`DEPLOYING` enum value), `next.config.ts` (ssh2 externalized), `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

### Schema (additive, `Agency*`-prefixed)
Built on the WIP additions. Enums `AgencyDealStage`, `AgencyActivityKind`, `AgencyQuoteStatus`, plus `DEPLOYING` added to `AgencyDemoStatus`. `AgencyProspect` gains `stage`, `dealValueCents`, `scrapeJson/scrapeStatus/scrapedAt`, relations `activities`/`client`. `AgencyDemoSite` gains `extractionJson`, `deployMode`, `bundleBytes`. New models `AgencyActivity`, `AgencyClient`, `AgencyQuote`, `AgencyQuoteLineItem`.

### SSRF protections
https/http only; DNS-resolves the host and refuses if **any** resolved address is non-public — loopback `127/8`/`::1`, private `10/8`/`172.16/12`/`192.168/16`/`fc00::/7`, link-local + metadata `169.254/16` (incl. `169.254.169.254`)/`fe80::/10`, CGNAT `100.64/10`, multicast/reserved `224/4`/`240/4`/`ff00::/8`, unspecified `::`, and IPv4-mapped/NAT64 IPv6 embedding a private v4. Manual redirects (≤3), each hop re-parsed + re-validated. ~2MB streamed-and-truncated body cap, ~10s timeout, descriptive UA, no headless browser. Guard helpers are pure + exported + unit-tested. Operator-triggered only; degrades to the deterministic generator without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

### Deploy gating
`deployDemo` builds the bundle, then default-OFF records `DEPLOYED_STUB` + intended `slug.agency.revsports.ca` + bundle bytes (provisions nothing); only with `agency_deploy_enabled=true` does it enqueue a real deploy (`DEPLOYING`) — no live infra touched by this build.

### Build / test result
- `npx prisma generate`: clean.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: **0 errors**. Webpack compilation: clean.
- `test/agency-phase2.test.ts` (SSRF guards incl. private-IP refusal + redirect re-validation + size/timeout caps, extraction parsing, pipeline transitions, quote math, deploy bundle): **all pass**. Full suite went 958→984 tests; the **7 failures are pre-existing** (verified identical on the baseline via stash — all in untouched files like `lib/actions-contact.ts`); my work adds **0 new failures**.

One important note on `npm run build`: after fixing the pre-existing `ssh2` native-addon bundling error (added `ssh2` to `serverExternalPackages` — standard Next.js treatment, no runtime change), the build compiles and type-checks fully, then fails **only** at the static-prerender step for pre-existing DB-backed marketing pages (`/tools`, `/features`) with `Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL`. That is purely environmental — the isolated worktree has no DB and the rules forbid me from providing one (no `prisma db push`, no pointing at prod). None of the Sitewave pages are affected (all `force-dynamic`). In the normal build environment where `DATABASE_URL` is set, this step passes.
